title: Chapter 1 Quiz
description: Test your knowledge of cloud fundamentals and AWS basics.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT one of the five essential characteristics of cloud computing?
questions.explanation: Resource pooling means the hardware is shared (multi-tenant). Dedicated hardware for each customer would be a private cloud, not a public cloud trait.

questions.question: What does 'rapid elasticity' in cloud computing refer to?
options: Resources scaling up and down automatically based on demand
questions.explanation: Rapid elasticity allows you to quickly provision and de-provision resources to match demand exactly.

questions.question: The cloud service model where you manage the operating system and applications is:
questions.explanation: Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS) gives you control over the OS and middleware. With PaaS you only manage the application; with SaaS you manage nothing.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of Platform as a Service (PaaS)?
questions.explanation: Elastic Beanstalk lets you upload code and it handles deployment, scaling, and OS management – that’s PaaS.

questions.question: In a public cloud, the infrastructure is shared among multiple organisations.
questions.explanation: True. Multi-tenancy is a defining feature of public cloud, though data and resources are isolated.

questions.question: Which deployment model combines on-premises infrastructure with public cloud?
questions.explanation: Hybrid cloud connects private infrastructure (on-premises or hosted) with public cloud services.

questions.question: AWS Outposts is a service that enables hybrid cloud by bringing AWS hardware into your data centre.
questions.explanation: True. Outposts provides the same AWS APIs and infrastructure on-premises for a truly consistent hybrid experience.

questions.question: What are the two core AWS services launched in 2006?
questions.explanation: Simple Storage Service (S3) and Elastic Compute Cloud (EC2) were the first two services, launched in 2006.

questions.question: An AWS Region consists of at least how many Availability Zones?
questions.explanation: Each Region has at least two Availability Zones for high availability, though most have three or more.

questions.question: Which AWS infrastructure component caches content closer to end users?
questions.explanation: Edge Locations are used by CloudFront CDN to cache content, reducing latency for users globally.

questions.question: Cloud computing shifts spending from capital expenditure (CapEx) to ________ expenditure (OpEx).
questions.explanation: The correct term is operational expenditure (OpEx). This is the ‘pay-as-you-go’ model.

questions.question: Which benefit of cloud computing allows you to stop guessing infrastructure capacity?
questions.explanation: With cloud you can auto-scale, meaning you no longer need to over-provision or worry about traffic spikes manually.

questions.question: What does 'measured service' mean in the context of cloud computing?
options: Resource usage is monitored, controlled, and reported, providing transparency for both provider and consumer
You have to measure your own usage manually
questions.explanation: Measured service implies metering capability. You pay only for what you use, and you can see detailed billing.

questions.question: According to the Shared Responsibility Model, who is responsible for securing the physical data centres in IaaS?
questions.explanation: AWS is responsible for the security OF the cloud (physical, infrastructure). The customer is responsible for security IN the cloud (OS, apps, data).

questions.question: PaaS gives you the most control over the underlying operating system.
questions.explanation: False. IaaS gives you the most control; PaaS abstracts the OS away so you can focus on code.

questions.question: Gmail is a good example of which cloud service model?
questions.explanation: Software as a Service – you use the application without worrying about servers, storage, or networking.

questions.question: What does the term 'multi-tenancy' refer to?
options: Many customers sharing the same physical hardware
questions.explanation: Multi-tenancy means multiple customers (tenants) share the same underlying infrastructure, with isolation mechanisms in place.

questions.question: Which AWS service is used for content delivery and caching globally?
questions.explanation: Amazon CloudFront is a fast content delivery network (CDN) that uses Edge Locations to cache content near users.

questions.question: AWS Free Tier usage allows you to run a small EC2 instance for 12 months at no charge (within limits).
questions.explanation: True. The Free Tier includes 750 hours per month of t2.micro or t3.micro instance usage for 12 months.

questions.question: Which of the following is a key advantage of using a hybrid cloud approach?
options: It is always cheaper than public cloud
You get to own all the hardware
You can keep sensitive data on-premises while leveraging public cloud scalability
questions.explanation: Hybrid cloud allows you to meet data sovereignty requirements while still using public cloud for burst capacity.

questions.question: The five essential characteristics of cloud computing were defined by ________.
questions.explanation: The National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) published the widely accepted definition.

questions.question: An Availability Zone can consist of multiple data centres, but they are treated as a single logical building.
questions.explanation: False. An AZ can be one or more discrete data centres, but they are physically separated enough that a failure in one won’t affect others in the same AZ.

questions.question: What does OpEx stand for?
questions.explanation: OpEx = Operational Expenditure. It’s the ongoing cost for running day-to-day business, as opposed to capital expenditure.

questions.question: Why can cloud providers offer lower prices due to 'massive economies of scale'?
options: They buy resources in such bulk that unit costs plummet
questions.explanation: By purchasing compute, storage, and networking equipment at enormous volumes, AWS gets discounts they pass on to you.

questions.question: You deploy a web application and only want to manage your code and data, not the server. Which model should you choose?
questions.explanation: PaaS abstracts the server layer; you simply deploy your app and the platform handles everything else.
